name: mod_info
description: The running mod's identity and health: mod_id, mod_version, assembly_version, informational_version, pipe_name (the local named pipe this game listens on, the sidecar's --pipe: tells which game a sidecar reached when two run on one machine), and methods: every method the mod answers, each {method, calls, errors, total_ms, mean_ms (null before the first call), max_ms} counted in memory since the mod loaded (main-thread time per request; errors are replies with ok false). Also count, reflection: [{member, resolved, optional}] (every game member the mod reaches by reflection and every Harmony target it patches; optional ones belong to other mods such as Terraforming Reloaded and BlueprintMod) and missing_count (required members not found: methods that need one answer game_changed). runtime (1.9.1+): what the mod has cost the game since it loaded: uptime_s; world_epoch (worlds left since load; leaving one clears IC pauses, job records, print and flight logs); request_budget_ms (main-thread ms per frame for requests, null = unlimited); frames {busy_frames, requests_served, requests_per_frame_mean, requests_per_frame_max, frame_ms, budget_stops (frames that left requests for the next one), expired (requests never reached before game_timeout)}; memory {gc_collections, gc_max_generation, gc_total_memory_bytes, mono_used_bytes, mono_heap_bytes (null where the game does not report them)}; methods: the 10 methods called so far that cost the most main-thread time, most first (1.14.0+; method_count counts them all), each {method, calls, errors, main_thread_ms, handler_ms, serialize_ms, queue_wait_ms, reply_bytes}, the last four as {total, mean, max}. The mod's own pipe reply envelope (read by pipe clients such as the script dashboard) also carries elapsed_ms, that request's main-thread time; MCP tool results do not carry it, so use the methods' mean_ms and max_ms here. Read only; no gateway is needed. 1.14.0+: by default the reply keeps the first entries of its lists (methods 15, reflection 10); truncated gives each cut list's returned and total counts, and list_limits {list: count} keeps more.
